files.lesson.md: --- order: 33 unit: error9 node: AC9M9M04 n3 uses: [AC9M9M04 n2] assumes: [AC9M9M04 n2] connection: photo-finish title: Percentage error summary: "Percentage error is relative error times 100. It lets you ask whether a difference is bigger than the measurement could be wrong by." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "Two swimmers finish a hundredth of a second apart. Is the result real?" --- Two swimmers' times differ by a hundredth of a second, and the timer is accurate to a thousandth. Is the result real, or could it be a measurement slip? Have a guess, and we'll come back to it at the end. (The times are made up for the task.) ## Predict: is the result real ```step stage: predict insight: "Choosing whether a 0.010 s gap is real when the timer error is 0.001 s shows whether students compare the difference with the measurement error." check: type: predict q: "Two times are 52.340 s and 52.350 s. Each is accurate to ±0.001 s. Is the 0.010 s gap real?" options: - "Yes: the gap is bigger than the largest possible error" - "No: 0.01 s is too small to notice" - "No: the timer might be wrong" - "Can't tell without a bigger gap" actual: "Yes. Each time could be out by 0.001 s, so the gap could be out by at most 0.002 s. The gap is 0.010 s, five times that." ``` ## Run: percentage error ```step stage: run insight: "Percentage error = relative error × 100, so a relative error of 0.002 is 0.2%." check: { type: number, q: "A relative error is $0.002$. What is the percentage error? (%)", answer: 0.2, tolerance: 0.001, explain: "0.002 × 100 = 0.2%." } ``` ## Investigate: as a percentage ```step stage: investigate insight: "Percentage error makes errors easy to compare and to quote. Multiply by 100 and add the % sign." tasks: - check: type: number q: "A timer is out by $0.001$ s on a $52.34$ s race. What is the percentage error? (%, 4 decimal places)" answer: 0.0019 tolerance: 0.0002 explain: "0.001 ÷ 52.34 = 0.0000191, × 100 = 0.0019%." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "What is $0.002 \\times 100$?", answer: 0.2, tolerance: 0.001, explain: "0.002 × 100 = 0.2." } - check: type: number q: "The gap between the swimmers is $0.010$ s. What percentage of $52.34$ s is that? (%, 3 decimal places)" answer: 0.019 tolerance: 0.002 explain: "0.010 ÷ 52.34 = 0.000191, × 100 = 0.019%." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#tia" text: "Tia finds the percentage error of a $20$ mm hole that is $0.04$ mm out. Click the line where her working goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: percent-error-no-100 explain: "Line 3: 0.002 is the relative error. Multiply by 100 to get 0.2%." ``` ### Percentage error ```worked \text{percentage error} = \dfrac{\text{absolute error}}{\text{true value}} \times 100\% :: Relative error as a percentage. 0.04 \div 20 = 0.002 :: The relative error. 0.002 \times 100 = 0.2\% :: The percentage error. \text{gap} > \text{combined error} \Rightarrow \text{result is real} :: Compare the difference with what the measurements could be out by. ``` ### Times 100 ### Find the mistake Read Tia's working. Which line forgets the percentage? ## Modify: a bigger gap or a bigger error ```step stage: modify insight: "Whether a difference is real depends on how big it is compared with the error." tasks: - hint: ["Each time may be out by 0.001.", "Together they could be out by 0.002."] check: { type: number, q: "Two times are each accurate to $\\pm 0.001$ s. By how much could the gap between them be out, at most? (s)", answer: 0.002, tolerance: 0.0001, explain: "0.001 + 0.001 = 0.002 s." } - hint: ["The gap is 0.010 s.", "Compare with 0.020 s."] check: { type: question, q: "The same race is timed by a stopwatch accurate to $\\pm 0.01$ s each. The gap is still $0.010$ s. Is it real?", options: ["Not necessarily: the gap could be out by 0.02 s, more than the gap itself", "Yes: the gap is the same", "Yes: 0.01 is exact", "No: the stopwatch is wrong"], answer: 0, feedback: [null, "The error is now bigger than the gap.", "A reading isn't exact.", "The stopwatch isn't wrong, just less precise."], explain: "Combined error 0.02 s is bigger than the 0.010 s gap, so the order could be reversed." } - hint: ["Find the percentage of 50.", "0.05 ÷ 50 × 100."] check: { type: number, q: "A length of $50$ cm is out by $0.05$ cm. What is the percentage error? (%)", answer: 0.1, tolerance: 0.001, explain: "0.05 ÷ 50 = 0.001, × 100 = 0.1%." } ``` ### The gap could be out by ### A cruder timer ### A length ## Practise: percentage error ```step stage: practise insight: "Turning an absolute error into a percentage." tasks: - check: type: number q: "A length is 50 cm and out by 1 cm. What is the percentage error? (%)" answer: 2 explain: "1 ÷ 50 × 100 = 2%." - check: type: number q: "A mass of 200 g is out by 5 g. What is the percentage error? (%)" answer: 2.5 tolerance: 0.01 explain: "5 ÷ 200 × 100 = 2.5%." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "What is $5 \\div 200$?", answer: 0.025, tolerance: 0.0005, explain: "5 ÷ 200 = 0.025." } - check: type: number q: "Review: a hole should be 20 mm and measures 20.04 mm. What is the absolute error? (mm)" answer: 0.04 tolerance: 0.001 explain: "20.04 − 20 = 0.04." ``` ### Length ### Mass ### Review ## Make: the photo finish ```step stage: make insight: "Returning to the swimmers: decide if the result is real by comparing the gap with the combined error." tasks: - hint: ["The gap is 0.010. The combined error is 0.002.", "How many times bigger?"] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "Two swimmers' times differ by 0.010 s. Each time is accurate to ±0.001 s. How many times bigger is the gap than the largest possible error in the gap? (made up for the task)" steps: - ["largest error in the gap $= 0.001 + 0.001 = 0.002$", "the errors could add"] - ["$0.010 \\div 0.002 = 5$", "how many times bigger"] - ["so the result is real", "the gap is bigger than the error"] answer: "5" answerLabel: "Times bigger" tolerance: 0.001 feedback: - ["10", "That compares with one error. The gap's error is both times' errors added: 0.002."] - ["0.002", "That's the largest error. Compare the gap with it."] criteria: - "I added the two errors." - "I divided the gap by the combined error." - "I said whether the result is real." explain: "0.010 ÷ 0.002 = 5, so the gap is five times the largest possible error: the order is real." - check: type: question q: "What would make you doubt the result?" options: ["A timer much less precise, with an error as big as the gap", "A winner by a clear second", "A timer accurate to 0.001 s", "A long race"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "A big gap is easy to trust.", "That's the case where we trust it.", "Length alone doesn't matter."] explain: "If the combined error is as big as the gap, you can't say who won." ``` ### Is it real ### What would worry you **Also used in** - **Sport.** Photo finishes and timing records need the timer's accuracy. - **Science.** Whether an effect is bigger than the noise in the measurement. - **Next unit.** Models of proportions and rates. ```teacher summary: Students find a percentage error and use it to decide whether a difference is bigger than the measurement could be wrong by (AC9M9M04, node 3). time: 35 timing: Predict and Run 6 min · Investigate 10 min · Modify 8 min · Practise and Make 11 min goals: - I can find the percentage error. - I can compare a difference with the combined error. - I can say if a result is real. struggle: "Forgetting ×100. Ask: is 0.002 a percentage?" before: > Students need Absolute and relative error. The one idea: a difference is only believable if it is bigger than the errors that could add up to produce it. The swimmers' times are made up for the task. running: - "Predict: show of hands before the check." - "Paper: the photo finish in Make is worked on paper first." stuck: - see: A student says the gap is within error because 0.01 is small. ask: Small compared with what? fix: "Compare it with the largest possible error in the gap: 0.002." stretch: How precise must a timer be to separate times 0.002 s apart? support: A printed number line with the error bars. leads: | Continues AC9M9M04 node 3. Where it leads: Proportion and rate models. exit: q: A length of 200 cm is out by 1 cm. What is the percentage error? a: 0.5%. explain: | Percentage error is the absolute error divided by the true value, times 100. A difference is real only if it is bigger than the combined errors. ```
